defined as the movement of one coulomb of charge past any given point of a conductor during
one second of time.

sources.text:
In humans, as in all mammals, the mature RBC lacks a nucleus. This allows the cell more room to store
hemoglobin, the oxygen-binding protein, enabling the RBC to transport more oxygen. RBCs are also biconcave
in shape; this shape increases their surface area for the diffusion of oxygen across their surfaces. In non-
mammalian vertebrates such as birds and fish, mature RBCs do have a nucleus.
